en: Taal Volcano erupts liquid magma that cools into solid igneous rock.
Halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture of solid ingredients suspended in sweetened liquid milk.
Squeezing a calamansi fruit causes a chemical change when its acidic juice reacts with baking soda.
Water dripping in the Puerto Princesa Underground River deposits dissolved minerals to form solid stalactites.
Milling harvested sugarcane extracts solid sucrose that dissolves in water to form a homogeneous solution.
The steel body of a Manila jeepney is a solid mixture of iron and carbon atoms.
The feathers of a Philippine Eagle are made of keratin, a strong solid protein material.
Melting solid tablea cacao in hot water is a physical change because no new substance forms.
The sand along Manila Bay is a heterogeneous mixture of tiny solid rock and shell fragments.
Piña fibers woven into a Barong Tagalog are solid plant materials that do not dissolve in water.
Liquid water in Lake Taal changes into a gaseous state through evaporation under the hot sun.
The bronze statue of Jose Rizal undergoes a chemical change when its surface oxidizes into green patina.
